verses.1: God said to Jacob, "Arise, go up to Bethel and live there. Build an altar to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau."
verses.2: Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, "Remove the foreign gods from among you, purify yourselves, and change your clothes."
verses.3: "We will prepare and go up to Bethel. There I will build an altar to the God who answered me in my time of trouble and has been with me on the road I have walked."
verses.4: They gave Jacob all the foreign gods they had in their possession, along with the earrings in their ears. Jacob buried them under the terebinth tree at Shechem.
verses.5: They set out, and the God of the cities around them became hostile, but they did not pursue the sons of Jacob.
verses.6: Jacob came to Luz in the land of Canaan, which is Bethel, and there with all the people who were with him.
verses.7: He built an altar there and named the place El Bethel, for there the gods revealed themselves to him as he fled from his brother.
verses.8: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and was buried under the terebinth at Bethel. Jacob named the place Alon Bachut.
verses.9: God appeared to Jacob again as he came from Paddan Aram, and blessed him.
verses.10: God said to him, "Your name is Jacob. You will not be called Jacob anymore, but Israel will be your name." And he named him Israel.
verses.11: God said to him, "I am God Almighty. Increase and multiply. A nation and a company of nations will come from you, and kings will issue from your loins.
verses.12: And the land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give to you and to your offspring after you."
verses.13: And God ascended from the place where he had spoken with him.
verses.14: Jacob set up a pillar at the place where he had spoken with him. He poured a libation over it and anointed it with oil.
verses.15: Jacob named the place where God had spoken with him there El Bethel.
verses.16: They set out from Bethel, and while they were still a distance from the land of Ephrath, Rachel went into labor and struggled in childbirth.
verses.17: As she struggled in childbirth, the midwife said to her, "Do not fear, for this too is a son for you."
verses.18: When her life was in danger, she named him Ben-Oni, but his father named him Benjamin.
verses.19: Rachel died and was buried along the road to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).
verses.20: Jacob set up a pillar on her grave, and it remains the Pillar of Rachel's Burial to this day.
verses.21: Israel moved on and pitched his tent beyond Migdol Edar.
verses.22: While Israel was living in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine. Israel heard about it, and the sons of Jacob were twelve in number.
verses.23: Leah's sons, the firstborn of Jacob: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
verses.25: Bilhah, Rachel's servant, bore Dan and Naphtali.
verses.26: Zilpah, Leah's servant, bore Gad and Asher. These were the sons of Jacob born to him in Paddan Aram.
verses.27: Jacob came to Isaac his father at Mamre, in the city of Arba, which is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had dwelled.
verses.29: He breathed his last and died, an old man and full of years. He was gathered to his people. His sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: "You will not be called Jacob anymore, but Israel will be your name" — the name change is a key moment in Jacob's transformation into Israel; the rendering follows the Hebrew without adding theological interpretation.
- v. 18: "Ben-Oni" is translated as "son of sorrow" to reflect the emotional context of the naming.
- v. 19: "Ephrath" is rendered as "Ephrath" rather than "Ephrathah" to avoid redundancy with the parenthetical explanation of Bethlehem.
- v. 20: "Pillar of Rachel's Burial" is a direct rendering of מַצֶּבֶת קְבֻֽרַת־רָחֵל, with no added interpretation.
raw:
[1] God said to Jacob, "Arise, go up to Bethel and live there. Build an altar to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau."

[2] Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, "Remove the foreign gods from among you, purify yourselves, and change your clothes."

[3] "We will prepare and go up to Bethel. There I will build an altar to the God who answered me in my time of trouble and has been with me on the road I have walked."

[4] They gave Jacob all the foreign gods they had in their possession, along with the earrings in their ears. Jacob buried them under the terebinth tree at Shechem.

[5] They set out, and the God of the cities around them became hostile, but they did not pursue the sons of Jacob.

[6] Jacob came to Luz in the land of Canaan, which is Bethel, and there with all the people who were with him.

[7] He built an altar there and named the place El Bethel, for there the gods revealed themselves to him as he fled from his brother.

[8] Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and was buried under the terebinth at Bethel. Jacob named the place Alon Bachut.

[9] God appeared to Jacob again as he came from Paddan Aram, and blessed him.

[10] God said to him, "Your name is Jacob. You will not be called Jacob anymore, but Israel will be your name." And he named him Israel.

[11] God said to him, "I am God Almighty. Increase and multiply. A nation and a company of nations will come from you, and kings will issue from your loins.

[12] And the land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give to you and to your offspring after you."

[13] And God ascended from the place where he had spoken with him.

[14] Jacob set up a pillar at the place where he had spoken with him. He poured a libation over it and anointed it with oil.

[15] Jacob named the place where God had spoken with him there El Bethel.

[16] They set out from Bethel, and while they were still a distance from the land of Ephrath, Rachel went into labor and struggled in childbirth.

[17] As she struggled in childbirth, the midwife said to her, "Do not fear, for this too is a son for you."

[18] When her life was in danger, she named him Ben-Oni, but his father named him Benjamin.

[19] Rachel died and was buried along the road to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).

[20] Jacob set up a pillar on her grave, and it remains the Pillar of Rachel's Burial to this day.

[21] Israel moved on and pitched his tent beyond Migdol Edar.

[22] While Israel was living in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine. Israel heard about it, and the sons of Jacob were twelve in number.

[23] Leah's sons, the firstborn of Jacob: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.

[24] Rachel's sons: Joseph and Benjamin.

[25] Bilhah, Rachel's servant, bore Dan and Naphtali.

[26] Zilpah, Leah's servant, bore Gad and Asher. These were the sons of Jacob born to him in Paddan Aram.

[27] Jacob came to Isaac his father at Mamre, in the city of Arba, which is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had dwelled.

[28] Isaac lived 180 years.

[29] He breathed his last and died, an old man and full of years. He was gathered to his people. His sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

---
Notes
- v. 10: "You will not be called Jacob anymore, but Israel will be your name" — the name change is a key moment in Jacob's transformation into Israel; the rendering follows the Hebrew without adding theological interpretation.
- v. 18: "Ben-Oni" is translated as "son of sorrow" to reflect the emotional context of the naming.
- v. 19: "Ephrath" is rendered as "Ephrath" rather than "Ephrathah" to avoid redundancy with the parenthetical explanation of Bethlehem.
- v. 20: "Pillar of Rachel's Burial" is a direct rendering of מַצֶּבֶת קְבֻֽרַת־רָחֵל, with no added interpretation.
